policy.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) of the Spine
policy.text:
Scope of Policy

This Clinical Policy Bulletin addresses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) of the spine.

Note: Precertification may be required for select procedures and interventions. Use the CPT code search tool to see if precertification is required.

Medical Necessity

Aetna considers magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) of the spine medically necessary when any of the following criteria is met:

• Clinical evidence of spinal stenosis; or

• Clinical suspicion of a spinal cord or cauda equina compression syndrome; or

• Congenital anomalies or deformities of the spine; or

• Diagnosis and evaluation of lumbar epidural lipomatosis; or

• Evaluation of recurrent symptoms after spinal surgery; or

• Evaluation prior to epidural injection to rule out tumor or infection and to delineate the optimal anatomical location for performing the injection; or

• Follow-up of evaluation for spinal malignancy or spinal infection; or

• Known or suspected myelopathy (e.g., multiple sclerosis) for initial diagnosis when MRI of the brain is negative or symptoms mimic those of other spinal or brainstem lesions; or

• Known or suspected primary spinal cord tumors (malignant or non-malignant); or

• Persistent back or neck pain with radiculopathy as evidenced by pain plus objective findings of motor or reflex changes in the specific nerve root distribution, and no improvement after 6 weeks of conservative therapy*; or

• Primary spinal bone tumors or suspected vertebral, paraspinal, or intraspinal metastases; or

• Progressively severe symptoms despite conservative management; or

• Rapidly progressing neurological deficit, or major motor weakness; or

• Severe back pain (e.g., requiring hospitalization); or

• Spondylolisthesis and degenerative disease of the spine that has not responded to 4 weeks of conservative therapy*; or

• Suspected infectious process (e.g., osteomyelitis epidural abscess of the spine or soft tissue); or

• Suspected spinal cord injury secondary to trauma; or

• Suspected spinal fracture and/or dislocation secondary to trauma (if plain films are not conclusive); or

• Suspected transverse myelitis.

* Conservative therapy = moderate activity, analgesics, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, muscle relaxants.

Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven

• Aetna considers BoneMRI (MRI-based synthetic CT) experimental, investigational, or unproven for pre-operative assessments and surgical planning of the spine and the pelvis; and for diagnosing or monitoring of tumors (primary or metastatic).

• Aetna considers MRI and CT of the spine experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications because their clinical value for indications other than the ones listed above has not been established. Clinical guidelines, including those from the Agency for Healthcare Policy and Research, have consistently recommended against routine imaging studies for acute low back pain.

• Aetna considers the use of MRI for further evaluation of unstable injury in neurologically intact individuals with blunt trauma after a negative cervical spine CT result not medically necessary.

• Aetna considers dynamic-kinetic MRI experimental, investigational, or unproven for evaluation of the cervical spine because its effectiveness has not been established.

• Aetna considers the use of routine MRI after a normal CT of the cervical spine in obtunded or comatose individuals experimental, investigational, or unproven because the clinical value of this approach has not been established.

• Aetna considers dual-energy CT experimental, investigational, or unrpoven for the evaluation of bone marrow edema and fracture lines in acute vertebral fractures because the clinical value of this approach has not been established.

Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1 with objective findings.

matches.rationale: The rule requires clinical evidence of spinal stenosis, but the chart documents only lumbar radiculopathy without any mention of stenosis, so this indication route is not relevant to this patient.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The chart documents no suspicion of spinal cord or cauda equina compression syndrome, so this indication route is not applicable.

evidence.quote: Inspection shows no deformity.

matches.rationale: The chart documents no congenital spinal anomaly or deformity, so this indication rule does not apply.

evidence.quote: Assessment: Ongoing lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1 with objective findings.

matches.rationale: The chart documents lumbar radiculopathy, not lumbar epidural lipomatosis, so the indication rule does not apply.

evidence.quote: Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.

matches.rationale: The rule requires prior spinal surgery for recurrent symptoms evaluation; the chart shows no prior surgery, only a referral under consideration, so the rule does not apply.

evidence.quote: Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today 08/03/2026 to further evaluate disc pathology. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.

Plan: Continue NSAIDs as needed for symptom control. Recommend home exercise program. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The rule only supports coverage when the MRI is performed prior to an epidural injection to rule out tumor/infection and guide injection; the chart documents the MRI is being ordered for surgical evaluation, not for an epidural injection, so the indication is not present.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The chart contains no documentation of evaluation for spinal malignancy or infection, and the patient explicitly denies related symptoms, so the indication rule does not apply.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The rule requires known or suspected myelopathy, which is not documented in the chart.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The chart contains no documentation of known or suspected primary spinal cord tumor and explicitly denies cancer history, so this indication rule does not apply.

evidence.quote: Patient returns for pre-surgical evaluation; low back pain persists despite NSAID and PT.
Exam: Unchanged; neurologic exam shows 4/5 left great toe extension and diminished left ankle reflex.
NSAID therapy was started on 06/19/2026 and ended on 07/27/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/22/2026, completed 10 sessions by 07/27/2026, and showed no improvement.

matches.rationale: The rule requires 6 weeks of conservative therapy without improvement, but the patient only received 5.4 weeks, so the requirement is not met.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The rule requires documented suspicion of primary spinal bone tumor or metastasis, which is absent in the chart, making the rule not applicable.

evidence.quote: She reports low back pain persisting, unchanged in character.
She reports low back pain unchanged;
low back pain persists despite NSAID and PT.

matches.rationale: The chart shows persistent but unchanged low back pain, not progressively severe symptoms, so the rule is not met.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
Neurologic exam: strength 5/5 hip flexion bilaterally, 4/5 left great toe extension (motor weakness consistent with L5 radiculopathy).

matches.rationale: This red-flag indication does not apply because the chart documents no rapidly progressive neurologic deficit and only mild (4/5) motor weakness, not major motor weakness.

evidence.quote: She describes the pain as aching, localized to the lumbar region, worsened with prolonged sitting and forward flexion.
Assessment: Acute lumbar strain, likely muscular.
She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The rule is a red-flag indication for severe back pain requiring hospitalization, but the chart documents only acute lumbar strain with aching pain and no hospitalization or other red flags; thus this red-flag route does not apply, and coverage would depend on the conservative-care pathway.
The chart contains no documentation of spondylolisthesis or degenerative disease of the spine, so this indication rule is not relevant to the patient.
The chart contains no documentation of a suspected infectious process, so this indication route does not apply.

evidence.quote: She denies any trauma or neurologic symptoms.

matches.rationale: The rule requires suspected spinal cord injury secondary to trauma, but the chart explicitly documents no trauma and no suspicion of spinal cord injury.
The chart contains no documentation of suspected spinal fracture or dislocation secondary to trauma, so this indication rule does not apply.
The chart contains no mention of suspected transverse myelitis, so this indication is not relevant to this case.

evidence.quote: Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today 08/03/2026 to further evaluate disc pathology.

matches.rationale: The rule addresses BoneMRI (MRI‑based synthetic CT), but the ordered study is a standard lumbar MRI without contrast, so the exclusion does not apply.

evidence.quote: Objective radiculopathy findings include diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness.
Assessment: Ongoing lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1 with objective findings.

matches.rationale: The exclusion applies only to indications not listed in the policy; the chart documents objective radiculopathy, which is a recognized covered indication, so the rule does not apply to this case.

evidence.quote: She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

matches.rationale: The rule applies only to blunt trauma with neurologically intact status after a negative cervical spine CT, none of which are documented.
The rule addresses dynamic‑kinetic MRI of the cervical spine, while the ordered study is a static lumbar MRI, making the rule irrelevant to this case.
The rule applies only to routine MRI after a normal cervical CT in obtunded or comatose individuals; the chart shows a lumbar MRI with no cervical CT and the patient is alert and oriented.

evidence.quote: Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today 08/03/2026 to further evaluate disc pathology.

matches.rationale: The rule addresses dual‑energy CT, but the ordered study is a lumbar MRI, so the rule does not apply to this case.
